result.topic_en: An attempt at a new theory of decomposing cubes, i.e. analysing the equation a^3+b^3+c^3=0 by substitutions with sums and cube roots of unity (descent-type reduction), with related cubic and fifth-power identities.
result.transcription:
Math 16
Neue Theorie der Zerlegung der Cuben. [-44410-] (9)
Es sei $a^3+b^3+c^3=0$
Man setze
$a+b=p$
$a+c=q$
$b+c=r$
so wird
$(p+q+r)^3=24pqr$
$p,q,r$ sind unter sich untheilbar, eine von diesen Grossen aber muss durch 9 theilbar seyn. Man wird haben
$p=9P^3$
$q=Q^3$
$r=R^3$
$9P^3+Q^3+R^3=6PQR$
$(2P+\varepsilon Q+\varepsilon\varepsilon R)(2P+\varepsilon\varepsilon Q+\varepsilon R)(2P+Q+R)+P^3=0$
Setzt man
$2P+\varepsilon Q+\varepsilon\varepsilon R=A$
$2P+\varepsilon\varepsilon Q+\varepsilon R=B$
$2P+Q+R=C$
So wird
$-(A+B+C)^3=216ABC$
$A=\alpha^3,\ B=\beta^3,\ C=\gamma^3$
$\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3+6\alpha\beta\gamma=0$
$(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^3+(\alpha+\beta\varepsilon+\gamma\varepsilon\varepsilon)^3+(\alpha+\beta\varepsilon\varepsilon+\gamma\varepsilon)^3=0$
$9\alpha^3=(2\alpha-\beta\varepsilon\varepsilon-\gamma\varepsilon)(2\alpha-\beta\varepsilon-\gamma\varepsilon\varepsilon)(2\alpha-\beta-\gamma)$
$(p+q-r)^5+(q+r-p)^5+(r+p-q)^5=$ [-$p^5+q^5+r^5$-] $(p+q+r)^5$
$-80pqr\,(pp+qq+rr)$
[-$8PQR\ (P+Q-R)^3+(Q+R-P)^3+(R+P-Q)^3$-]
[-illegible-]
$(x+\varepsilon y+\varepsilon\varepsilon z)^3+(x+\varepsilon\varepsilon y+\varepsilon z)^3+(x+y+z)^3$
$=3x^3+3y^3+3z^3+18xyz$

methods.what: Substitution of pairwise sums transforms a^3+b^3+c^3=0 into (p+q+r)^3=24pqr
Coprimality and divisibility argument giving p=9P^3, q=Q^3, r=R^3 and the equation 9P^3+Q^3+R^3=6PQR
Factorisation of the cubic form using cube roots of unity epsilon
Transformed equation in A, B, C
Reduction to alpha^3+beta^3+gamma^3+6alpha beta gamma=0 and its expression as a sum of three cubes (descent)
Identity for the sum of cubes of the linear forms with cube roots of unity

items.quote: $p,q,r$ sind unter sich untheilbar, eine von diesen Grossen aber muss durch 9 theilbar seyn.
items.english: p, q, r are mutually coprime, but one of these quantities must be divisible by 9.
One will have p = 9P^3, q = Q^3, r = R^3.
